symbols.name: V
symbols.type: A finite set of observed vertices
symbols.role: Observed variables.

symbols.name: U
symbols.type: A finite set of latent vertices
symbols.role: Exogenous roots.

symbols.name: State
symbols.type: A family \(\{\mathcal X_i:i\in V\cup U\}\) of fixed finite state spaces
symbols.role: State spaces for all vertices.

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: A finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup U\)
symbols.role: The causal graph before latent projection.

symbols.name: X
symbols.role: Treatment vertices.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.role: Outcome vertices.

symbols.name: Ystar
symbols.role: The terminal outcome in the binary-sink slice.

symbols.name: x
symbols.role: Fixed treatment state.

symbols.name: y
symbols.role: Fixed outcome state.

symbols.name: W
symbols.role: Observed vertices remaining after treatment and outcome substitution.

symbols.name: CSI
symbols.type: A finite list \(\mathcal C\) of local whole-row context-specific independence constraints on \(G\)
symbols.role: Input row equalities with observed activation predicates.

symbols.name: RowQ
symbols.type: A family \(\mathcal R=\{\mathcal R_i:i\in V\}\) of equivalence classes of complete parent assignments
symbols.role: The connected row-equality quotient generated by \(\mathcal C\).

symbols.name: Theta
symbols.type: The product \(\Theta(G)\) of normalized finite conditional probability tables
symbols.role: The unconstrained parameter space.

symbols.name: theta
symbols.role: A structural-model parameter.

symbols.name: ModelClass
symbols.role: Strictly positive semi-Markovian models satisfying the observed-context row equalities.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.type: The observed probability vector \(F(\theta)=(P_{\theta}(V=\mathbf v):\mathbf v\in\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal X_i)\)
symbols.role: All observed cells in lexicographic order.

symbols.name: q
symbols.role: The fixed state-specific causal query.

symbols.name: Expr
symbols.type: The class \(\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) of total arithmetic observed-cell expressions
symbols.role: Permitted positive-denominator identifying formulas.

symbols.name: Partition
symbols.type: A finite partition \(\mathcal K\) of \(\prod_{i\in W}\mathcal X_i\)
symbols.role: The partition refining all substituted activation regions.

symbols.name: Trace
symbols.type: A finite sequence \(t\) of CSI-authorized edge deletions
symbols.role: A partial, possibly empty, deletion history.

symbols.name: H
symbols.type: The context graph \(H_{k,t}\) obtained from \(G\) on cell \(k\in\mathcal K\) along trace \(t\)
symbols.role: A graph on which context-compatible recovery is attempted.

symbols.name: District
symbols.type: A maximal bidirected-connected component \(D\) of \(\operatorname{An}_{H_{k,t}\setminus X}(Y)\)
symbols.role: A relevant confounded component.

symbols.name: Qfac
symbols.role: A district factor to be recovered or obstructed.

symbols.name: Success
symbols.role: A derivation of \(Q[D]_{k,t}\) from observed cells.

symbols.name: Forest
symbols.type: A nested pair \((F_{k,t,D},F'_{k,t,D})\) of rooted C-forests
symbols.role: A partial-trace graphical obstruction candidate.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.type: A strictly positive rational assignment \(\eta\) to every primitive coordinate outside the rows of \(Y_{\star}\)
symbols.role: The fixed nuisance table in the binary-sink slice.

symbols.name: pvec
symbols.role: The shared-row probabilities \(P(Y_{\star}=1\mid\text{row class }j)\).

symbols.name: Feta
symbols.role: The full observed-cell vector in the fixed-nuisance slice.

symbols.name: heta
symbols.role: The fixed interventional cell in the same slice.

symbols.name: ceta
symbols.role: The intercept of the observed-cell affine map.

symbols.name: Aeta
symbols.role: The trace- and forest-restricted coefficient matrix recomputed from structural syntax.

symbols.name: deta
symbols.role: The intercept of the query affine map.

symbols.name: betaeta
symbols.role: The trace- and forest-restricted coefficient vector of the query map.

symbols.name: hker
symbols.role: The canonical reduced-row-echelon kernel direction supported on the sink-row classes exposed by the forest.

symbols.name: pzero
symbols.role: A single positive shared-row baseline, not a countermodel pair.

symbols.name: eps
symbols.role: A perturbation radius bounded by coordinatewise positivity slack.

symbols.name: SliceCertificate
symbols.role: Independently checkable obstruction syntax containing no pair of models and no observed-law or unequal-query comparison.

symbols.name: SliceVerifier
symbols.role: The rational checker that recomputes the affine maps and the forest-supported kernel direction.

symbols.name: Handle
symbols.role: The starting technique for the unresolved global dichotomy.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.role: The candidate success-or-structural-certificate procedure.

symbols.name: Size
symbols.role: Here \(n=|V|+|U|\), \(m=|E(G)|\), \(c=|\mathcal C|\), \(K=\prod_{i\in W}|\mathcal X_i|\), \(R=\sum_{i\in V}|\mathcal R_i|\), \(o=\prod_{i\in V}|\mathcal X_i|\), and \(\ell\) is the largest input rational bit length.

symbols.name: Bound
symbols.role: A closed bound on structural branch syntax, expression size, and rational arithmetic.

symbols.name: ExampleFive
symbols.type: A pair \(\mathsf E_5=(\rho^+_5,\rho^-_5)\) of binary rational models
symbols.role: The five-node active-deletion boundary instance.

symbols.name: ExampleBow
symbols.role: The observed-reference-context bow boundary instance.

assumptions.condition: Every \(u\in U\) has no parent in \(G\).
Every \(u\in U\) has exactly two children, both in \(V\).

standard.name: Two-child latent restriction for semi-Markovian models

assumptions.condition: The variables indexed by \(U\) are mutually independent under \(\theta\).

standard.name: Independent exogenous roots in a semi-Markovian model

assumptions.condition: Every entry of every primitive conditional table in \(\theta\) is strictly positive.

novel.justification: This transparent scope condition describes finite stochastic mechanisms with full-support response noise, including randomized policy, diagnostic, and behavioral systems in which no recorded parent configuration makes a state impossible. It supplies a common open parameter domain for all conditional denominators and for two-sided perturbations around a positive baseline.

assumptions.condition: Every variable assigned by an activation predicate in \(\mathcal C\) belongs to \(V\), whether or not it is a root in \(G\).

novel.justification: The regime covers measured states that switch mechanisms after observed history, such as adherence after prior symptoms, a triage decision after recorded covariates, or a device mode selected from measured telemetry. These endogenous but observed switches fall outside control-variable results that require each switch to be a root.

assumptions.condition: Each relation in \(\mathcal C\) equates the complete conditional probability vectors of one child across the parent assignments declared irrelevant in its activation context.

novel.justification: The fixed-nuisance diagnostic slice isolates one recorded endpoint, as in a single failure or response outcome, without imposing singleton outcomes on the general completeness question.

assumptions.condition: Every state space indexed by \(V\cup U\) equals \(\{0,1\}\).

novel.justification: The slice covers binary treatments, endpoints, measured switches, and latent response types, and makes the initial shared-row lifting problem an exact rational linear problem.

assumptions.condition: The vertex \(Y_{\star}\) has no child in \(G\).

novel.justification: A terminal measured endpoint is natural in longitudinal causal graphs and makes each observed and interventional cell affine in its shared outcome-row probabilities.

assumptions.condition: Every coordinate of \(\eta\) is rational, normalized, strictly positive, and constant on the quotient classes prescribed by \(\mathcal R\).

novel.justification: Finite rational nuisance mechanisms include dense approximations to positive finite-state mechanisms and permit an independently reproducible exact base-case certificate.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal R\)
definitions.construction: For each \(i\in V\), form the finite graph whose vertices are complete assignments to \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\) and whose edges are exactly the whole-row equalities asserted by \(\mathcal C\); \(\mathcal R_i\) is the set of connected components of this graph.

definitions.name: \(\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\)
definitions.construction: The smallest class containing rational constants and coordinates of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), closed under finite sums, differences, products, and division by an expression whose strict positivity on \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)\) is recorded in the derivation syntax.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal K\)
definitions.construction: Substitute \(\mathbf x\) and \(\mathbf y\) into every activation predicate in \(\mathcal C\), encode each remaining predicate by its truth table on \(\prod_{i\in W}\mathcal X_i\), and take the nonempty fibers of the joint truth-table map.

definitions.name: \(t\)
definitions.construction: A finite, possibly empty, sequence of distinct edge identifiers; each entry records a relation in \(\mathcal C\), a cell \(k\in\mathcal K\) on which its substituted activation table is constantly true, the authorized edge, and the observed-cell indices retained for recovery.

definitions.name: \(H_{k,t}\)
definitions.construction: Start from \(G\) and delete in order exactly the edges named by trace \(t\) whose recorded authorization is valid on cell \(k\in\mathcal K\).

definitions.name: \(Q[D]_{k,t}\)
definitions.construction: For a relevant district \(D\) of \(H_{k,t}\), sum the product of primitive conditional rows indexed by \(D\) over all latent roots entering \(D\), after restricting row arguments to assignments compatible with \(k\) and \(t\).

definitions.name: \(\delta_{k,t,D}\)
definitions.construction: A finite syntax tree beginning with indexed coordinates of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), applying only marginalization, conditioning with a recorded positive-denominator judgment, district restriction, leaf removal, and substitutions whose CSI identifiers occur in \(t\), and ending with every coordinate of \(Q[D]_{k,t}\).

definitions.name: \((F_{k,t,D},F'_{k,t,D})\)
definitions.construction: Choose encoded vertex and edge subsets \(F_{k,t,D}\subseteq F'_{k,t,D}\subseteq H_{k,t}\) that each have one bidirected district, give every observed vertex at most one directed child, and have the same childless set \(R_0\), with \(F_{k,t,D}\cap X=\varnothing\), \(F'_{k,t,D}\cap X\ne\varnothing\), and \(R_0\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{H_{k,t}\setminus X}(Y)\).

definitions.name: \((c_{\eta},A_{\eta,t,F},d_{\eta},b_{\eta,t,F})\)
definitions.construction: Order the \(o\) observed cells and the \(r=|\mathcal R_{Y_{\star}}|\) outcome-row classes. Expand the finite latent sums using \(G\), the quotient \(\mathcal R\), the retained trace \(t\), its displayed forest \(F\), and the fixed nuisance table \(\eta\). Let \(J_{t,F}\) be the outcome-row classes reached by a root-to-‑\(Y_{\star}\) path inside the displayed forest and set all columns outside \(J_{t,F}\) to zero. Define \(c_{\eta}=F_{\eta}(0)\), \((A_{\eta,t,F})_{vj}=\mathbf 1\{j\in J_{t,F}\}\{F_{\eta}(e_j)_v-F_{\eta}(0)_v\}\), \(d_{\eta}=h_{\eta}(0)\), and \((b_{\eta,t,F})_j=\mathbf 1\{j\in J_{t,F}\}\{h_{\eta}(e_j)-h_{\eta}(0)\}\). Hence the restricted perturbation \(u\) has observed increment \(A_{\eta,t,F}u\) and query increment \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}u\). These coefficients are recomputed from the graph, quotient, retained forest trace, and fixed slice nuisance; neither observed-cell values nor countermodels are inputs.

definitions.name: \(h_{t,F}\)
definitions.construction: Run rational reduced-row-echelon elimination on the augmented row test \(A_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\lambda=b_{\eta,t,F}\). If it is inconsistent, choose the lexicographically first free column in the reduced system for \(A_{\eta,t,F}u=0\), set that free coordinate to the least positive integer clearing all denominators, set later free coordinates to zero, solve the pivot coordinates, and change the sign if necessary so that \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}u>0\); the resulting vector is \(h_{t,F}\). If the augmented system is consistent, return the symbol \(\mathsf{REJECT}\).

definitions.name: \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sink}}\)
definitions.construction: A finite string containing the activation-fiber truth table, one authorized retained trace, one rooted C-forest bitmask, the rational fixed nuisance table \(\eta\), one rational baseline \(p_0\in(0,1)^r\), and one rational \(\varepsilon>0\). It contains no second parameter table, no list of observed-cell equalities, and no comparison of two query values.

definitions.name: \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}\)
definitions.construction: Parse \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sink}}\); recompute the activation fibers, trace membership, quotient classes, and rooted C-forest predicate; check normalization, positivity, rationality, and quotient sharing of \(\eta\) and \(p_0\); recompute \(A_{\eta,t,F}\) and \(b_{\eta,t,F}\) by finite structural contraction; reject if \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\); otherwise recompute \(h_{t,F}\), check its forest support, and check \(0<\varepsilon<\min_{j:h_{t,F,j}\ne0}\min\{p_{0j},1-p_{0j}\}/|h_{t,F,j}|\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{sat}}\)
definitions.construction: Saturate context-compatible \(Q\)-factor recovery while carrying original observed-cell provenance and quotient row labels; retain every nonrepeating partial deletion trace; for each residual district extract rooted C-forest candidates and test whether their quotient-supported perturbation spaces survive all observed contractions before attempting multi-block gluing.

definitions.name: \(\mathsf{OCSI\text{-}ID}\)
definitions.construction: Compile \(\mathcal R\), construct the activation partition after substituting \(\mathbf x,\mathbf y\), enumerate the finite branch encodings prescribed by \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{sat}}\), and return a verifier-accepted total expression when recovery closes; in the fixed-nuisance binary-sink slice it may instead return a verifier-accepted \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sink}}\).

definitions.name: \(B(s)\)
definitions.construction: For \(s=(n,m,c,K,R,o,\ell)\), set \(T=\sum_{j=0}^{m}m!/(m-j)!\), \(D=2^n3^m\), \(F_0=3^{2n}4^{2m}\), \(N=2^{cK+R}TDF_0\), \(L=o(N+1)\), \(E=(o+8(L+1)^2)^{L+1}\), and \(M=2^{L+1}(\ell+\lceil\log_2(L+2)\rceil)\). Define \(B(s)=(N+1)(E+1)(o+R+1)^3(M+1)\). The factors encode activation truth tables and cells, quotient classes, nonrepeating trace states, factor states, nested forest bitmasks, expression directed acyclic graphs of at most \(L\) nodes, rational row reduction, and worst-case numerator and denominator bit growth.

definitions.name: \(\mathsf E_5\)
definitions.construction: The observed variables \(X,Z,Y\) and latent roots \(U,T\) are binary. The roots are independent with \(P(U=0)=P(T=0)=1/2\). The arrows are \(U\to X,U\to Y,T\to Z,T\to Y,X\to Z,Z\to Y\), and the CSI is \(Z\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}T\mid X=0\). In both models, \(P(X=0\mid U=0)=3/4\), \(P(X=0\mid U=1)=1/4\), \(P(Z=0\mid X=0,T)=1/2\), \(P(Z=0\mid X=1,T=0)=3/4\), and \(P(Z=0\mid X=1,T=1)=1/4\). In \(\rho^+_5\), every \(P(Y=1\mid U,T,Z)\) equals \(1/2\). In \(\rho^-_5\), every row with \(Z=1\) equals \(1/2\), while the \(Z=0\) rows ordered by \((U,T)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) equal \(53/100,53/100,57/100,1/4\). Complements give all unlisted binary probabilities. In both models, the observed table ordered by any \((x,z,y)\in\{0,1\}^3\) is \(P(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=1/8\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{bow}}\)
definitions.construction: The observed variables \(A,X,Y\) and latent root \(U\) are binary. The roots \(A,U\) are independent and fair; the arrows are \(A\to X,U\to X,U\to Y,X\to Y\); and the CSI is \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}U\mid A=0\). Set \(P(X=1\mid A=0,U)=1/2\), \(P(X=1\mid A=1,U=0)=1/4\), and \(P(X=1\mid A=1,U=1)=3/4\). The outcome rows \(P(Y=1\mid X,U)\) are \(1/5,3/5\) for \(X=0\) and \(2/5,4/5\) for \(X=1\), with each pair ordered by \(U=0,1\). Complements give all unlisted probabilities. The observed cells \((P(A=a,X=x,Y=0),P(A=a,X=x,Y=1))\) are \((3/20,1/10)\), \((1/10,3/20)\), \((7/40,3/40)\), and \((3/40,7/40)\) for \((a,x)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), respectively.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta(G)\), the table \(\theta\) satisfies all equalities in \(\mathcal C\) if and only if each child row is constant on every class of \(\mathcal R_i\). Replacing \(\mathcal C\) by \(\mathcal R\) preserves \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)\), the map \(\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}(V)\), and \(q(\theta)\).
statements.justification: The quotient removes syntactic overlap while preserving the exact observational fiber and causal target.
statements.gap: Pensar et al. and Duarte and Solus study context-specific representations rather than preservation of latent causal-query fibers and obstruction syntax.
statements.consumer: The quotient gives \(Y_0\) one canonical parameter index for exact deduplication and checking.

statements.statement: If recorded SUCCESS derivations cover every relevant district and their context contractions assemble \(E\in\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), then \(E(P_{\theta}(V))=q(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)\); every recorded divisor is strictly positive on this class.
statements.justification: The positive branch must return a total observed-cell formula with checked denominators.
statements.gap: Tikka et al. and Chen and Darwiche prove sound search rules but not sound assembly for this provenance-carrying exhaustive normal form.
statements.consumer: The result lets \(Y_0\) emit an auditable symbolic estimand rather than a bare verdict.

statements.statement: Under the fixed-nuisance binary-sink restrictions, the structural contractions in \(\texttt{def:fixed-sink-linearization}\) are rational and satisfy \(F_{\eta}(p+u)-F_{\eta}(p)=A_{\eta,t,F}u\) and \(h_{\eta}(p+u)-h_{\eta}(p)=b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}u\) for every perturbation \(u\) supported on \(J_{t,F}\) with \(p,p+u\in(0,1)^r\). The intercepts are \(c_{\eta}=F_{\eta}(0)\) and \(d_{\eta}=h_{\eta}(0)\).
statements.justification: The graph, quotient, and retained forest trace determine the exact observed and interventional linear maps, including their intercepts.
statements.gap: Generic polynomial encodings do not isolate this quotient-shared terminal-row affine slice with a trace-supported column set.
statements.consumer: The map is the exact rational base case for \(Y_0\)'s negative-certificate checker.

statements.statement: For every retained rooted C-forest \(F\) in the fixed-nuisance binary-sink slice, exactly one rational row-space alternative holds. If \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\), rational elimination returns \(\lambda\) with \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_{\eta,t,F}\), and the forest is structurally rejected. Otherwise \(\texttt{def:canonical-forest-kernel}\) returns a nonzero \(h_{t,F}\) supported on \(J_{t,F}\) such that \(A_{\eta,t,F}h_{t,F}=0\) and \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}h_{t,F}>0\).
statements.justification: The lemma makes the forest load-bearing by restricting the tested columns, while row-space membership rejects forests neutralized by shared reference contexts.
statements.gap: Classical hedge constructions do not impose CSI quotient sharing, and generic null-space tests do not tie the perturbation support to a retained forest trace.
statements.consumer: The result gives \(Y_0\) a deterministic forest-to-perturbation compiler or a structural rejection record.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sink}})=1\), let \(p^{+}=p_0+\varepsilon h_{t,F}\) and \(p^{-}=p_0-\varepsilon h_{t,F}\). The verified positivity bound gives \(p^{+},p^{-}\in(0,1)^r\). Combining either vector with the single fixed nuisance table \(\eta\) decodes two globally normalized, strictly positive, quotient-shared models in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ocsi}}(G,\mathcal C)\). The identity \(A_{\eta,t,F}h_{t,F}=0\) implies \(P_{p^{+},\eta}(V)=P_{p^{-},\eta}(V)\), while \(h_{\eta}(p^{+})-h_{\eta}(p^{-})=2\varepsilon b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}h_{t,F}>0\). Consequently the fixed query is not identified in this slice.
statements.justification: Soundness constructs the global pair from one baseline and a forest-derived kernel vector rather than storing semantic countermodels or their conclusions in the certificate.
statements.gap: Classical hedge completeness constructs unconstrained pairs, while generic algebraic verifiers can check supplied pairs without deriving them from a CSI-compatible forest.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives \(Y_0\) a compact, portable negative certificate for the first exact shared-row slice.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{sat}}\) be completed for every finite \((G,\mathcal C,\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\) so that exhaustive sound context-factor recovery either assembles a total \(E\in\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), or produces retained partial-trace rooted C-forests whose jointly quotient-supported multi-block contraction has a kernel direction with zero full observed increment and nonzero query increment, with the binary-sink construction as its exact one-block base case? The resulting procedure must be sound and complete, and on the maximal-regular observed-root subclass it must reduce to the Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash criterion while strictly covering inputs with observed endogenous activation.
statements.justification: This is the unresolved completeness kernel: multi-district local failures must glue through shared rows into a genuine global query-changing direction or force total arithmetic recovery.
statements.gap: Tikka et al. leave general CSI completeness unresolved; Mokhtarian et al. require observed root controls; Chen and Darwiche provide no complete state-specific obstruction theorem.
statements.consumer: A positive answer is the missing mathematical basis for a total explanatory CSI-identification backend in \(Y_0\).

statements.statement: For \(\mathsf E_5\), both displayed models have \(P(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=1/8\) for all \(x,z,y\in\{0,1\}\), while \(P_{X=0}^{\rho^+_5}(Y=1)=1/2\) and \(P_{X=0}^{\rho^-_5}(Y=1)=97/200\), giving the exact gap \(3/200\). Deleting the active edge \(T\to Z\) leaves the front-door graph \(X\to Z\to Y\) with \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), which has no hedge, whereas the empty trace retains \(F=\{Y\}\subset F'=\{X,Z,Y\}\) and the displayed difference of outcome rows lies in the corresponding observed kernel. For \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{bow}}\), the reference context gives \(P_{X=0}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=0,Y=1)=2/5\) and \(P_{X=1}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=1,Y=1)=3/5\). Thus the two query coefficient vectors lie in the row space of the full observed-cell matrix, so \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}\) structurally rejects the local \(A=1\) bow forest before any countermodel is formed.
statements.justification: The exact pair tests both required boundaries: active pruning can erase the obstruction, while a reference context can annihilate a local forest through row-space gluing.
statements.gap: Chen and Darwiche give a qualitative pruning warning; these rational fixtures impose two-child latents, positivity, an exact \(3/200\) gap, and structural reference-context rejection.
statements.consumer: The tables are deterministic fixtures for \(Y_0\)'s trace retention, rational contraction, and row-space rejection logic.

statements.statement: When \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), the activation partition has one cell, every authorized trace is empty, and the SUCCESS syntax and rooted C-forest predicate reduce to the Shpitser--Pearl \(\mathrm{ID}\) recursion and hedge syntax, respectively. Any complete resolution of \(\texttt{oeq:global-context-factor-dichotomy}\) must therefore return the ordinary \(Q\)-factor formula exactly when \(\mathrm{ID}\) succeeds and the ordinary hedge exactly when it fails.
statements.justification: The no-CSI case anchors every new syntactic object to the classical complete theory.
statements.gap: Shpitser and Pearl settle ordinary identification; the reduction ensures that observed-context syntax is conservative rather than an analogue on a new class.
statements.consumer: Existing \(Y_0\) ordinary-identification tests become exact regression tests for the new backend.

statements.statement: For every finite encoded input of size \(s\), construction of the activation truth table, quotient, all nonrepeating trace states, factor states, nested forest candidates, SUCCESS expression directed acyclic graphs of size at most \(L=o(N+1)\), and every rational binary-sink row-space certificate requires at most \(B(s)\) branches, symbols, and rational arithmetic operations; every such returned expression or slice certificate has encoding length at most \(B(s)\). This bounds the finite search space but does not assert that the unresolved global dichotomy selects a complete output on general multi-block inputs.
statements.justification: A closed normal-form bound separates finite structural enumeration from the open global gluing theorem.
statements.gap: Tikka et al. prove hardness and terminating sound search, while Mokhtarian et al. cover fixed root controls; neither gives this explicit endogenous-activation structural encoding bound.
statements.consumer: The bound gives \(Y_0\) a serialization ceiling and a deterministic budget for the verified binary-sink module.

sampling_model.design: Finite semi-Markovian structural causal model with observed-context whole-row CSI constraints; identification is population-level and introduces no sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: One population law on the fixed finite state space \(\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal X_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention is \(\operatorname{do}(X=\mathbf x)\), and the outcome cell is \(Y=\mathbf y\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive CPT entry is strictly positive as an explicit technical scope condition; each derived divisor also carries its own positivity judgment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the identification kernel; a returned observed-cell functional passes to downstream estimation.

estimand_functional: \(E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=P_{\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)\) or, in the certified binary-sink slice, \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sink}})=1\)

tldr: Fixed treatment and outcome assignments activate observed CSI information that variable-level identification can discard, but a local forest alone need not survive shared rows across contexts. The settled base case is a fixed-nuisance binary-sink certificate: the graph, row quotient, retained trace, and forest determine rational observed and query maps; row-space failure constructs a forest-supported kernel direction, and a single positive baseline plus an explicit radius yields two global shared-row models. The certificate stores neither model pair nor asserted observed or query comparisons. The field-tier kernel remains the open global context-factor dichotomy needed to extend this construction to coupled CPT blocks and obtain a complete arithmetic-formula-or-structural-obstruction procedure for observed endogenous activations.

project_justification.gap: Tikka et al. give sound CSI calculus and show that separate context graphs are incomplete. Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls, not observed endogenous activations. Chen and Darwiche give sound state-specific procedures without a complete obstruction theorem, and a local forest can be neutralized by cross-context row sharing.
project_justification.niche: Observed endogenous activation permits finite truth-table refinement while retaining shared CPT rows, reference-context recovery, cancellation, and information loss under active pruning.
project_justification.fill: The project first certifies the exact binary-sink lifting step through a forest-restricted row-space alternative and baseline perturbation, then asks whether provenance-carrying Q-factor recovery and partial traces force an analogous global multi-block dichotomy.

related_work: Boutilier et al. define local CSI through equality of conditional behavior, and Pensar et al. encode such equalities by labels; these works inform the canonical quotient. Shpitser and Pearl establish ordinary formula-or-hedge completeness, recovered when the CSI list is empty. Tikka et al., Theorems 5--6, prove sound CSI search and show that separate context-graph identification is insufficient; the proposed global dichotomy would add necessity. Mokhtarian et al., Theorem 1, prove an if-and-only-if criterion for maximal-regular labels activated by observed roots; roothood is essential to their conditioning reduction, so observed endogenous activations form a strict target domain rather than an attribution to that result. Chen and Darwiche, Theorem 1 and Proposition 5, supply a sound state-specific procedure and an active-pruning warning but no general completeness theorem. Their circuit work and Duarte et al.'s sharp polynomial programs inform finite algebraic contraction but do not provide a forest-derived shared-row kernel. Kivva et al. supply a positivity-aware generalized-identification comparator. Duarte and Solus characterize fully observed context-specific representations rather than latent query fibers. Bhattacharya et al. provide downstream estimation after a functional is returned, and the \(Y_0\) paper supplies the direct software consumer.
technical_internal_limitation: A rooted C-forest is not by itself a nonidentification certificate under shared CSI rows. In the reference-context bow, the \(A=0\) cells place the query coefficient in the observed row space and force structural rejection. Maximal active deletion also fails: in the five-node rational pair, the pruned graph has no hedge although the empty trace carries a kernel direction with query gap \(3/200\). The global theorem must therefore retain partial traces and prove a forest-supported kernel statement after all cross-context contractions; generic real-algebraic fiber testing does not supply this linkage or total arithmetic descent.
honest_scope: The canonical quotient, SUCCESS soundness, fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine map, forest-to-kernel row-space alternative, baseline perturbation soundness theorem, finite structural bound, and two rational boundary fixtures are supporting results. The global context-factor dichotomy is visibly open and remains the completeness kernel. No general certificate-soundness or complete procedure is claimed before multi-block forest lifting is established. Strict primitive-CPT positivity and observed endogenous activation are transparent novel scope conditions. With no CSI, the syntax reduces to ordinary \(\mathrm{ID}\); on observed root activations, any complete answer must reproduce the published maximal-regular criterion. Estimation is downstream.

novelty_justification: The field-tier question is stronger than sound CSI search, strictly targets a domain beyond complete observed-root control, and seeks necessity for state-specific identification. Its established first slice replaces a promissory semantic pair by a forest-restricted rational row-space test, a canonical kernel direction, and an explicit positivity-controlled baseline perturbation. The reference-context bow is rejected because its query vector lies in the observed row space, so forests cannot survive merely as decorative witnesses.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Complete state-specific identification under observed-context CSIs. In finite positive semi-Markovian DAGs, require every CSI activation variable to be observed and substitute the fixed treatment/outcome assignments before partitioning contexts. Construct a terminating sound-and-complete procedure returning either an arithmetic observed-cell formula for P_x(y), or a verified observed LC-certificate: an activation-refining partition, CSI-authorized deletion traces, SUCCESS ID-Qfunc derivations or OBSTRUCTION rooted C-forest pairs for every relevant c-component, and two global positive algebraic CPT tables indexed by the input CSI row-equality quotient that induce the same P(V) but different queries. Prove global shared-row gluing, total formula recovery or a genuine forest obstruction, and finite complexity; generic real-algebraic decision without the context/C-forest characterization does not count. Use Chen-Darwiche 2026, Tikka et al. 2019, and Mokhtarian et al. 2022 as anchors, and Y0 as the software consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The observed-context restriction removes an exact hidden-activation obstruction. Global CSI CPT rows reduce to connected equality classes, and fixed-nuisance binary-sink countermodels reduce exactly to a rational row-space/nullspace test. Two positive rational examples were checked, with query gaps 1/30 and 3/200. Active pruning, shared-row identification, cancellation, positive denominators, fixed cardinalities, and empty-trace decoration were attacked; saturated local-forest reasoning fails, but the literal partial-trace/global-witness certificate survives. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the finite global context-factor dichotomy: exhaustive sound reductions must yield a total arithmetic formula or partial-trace rooted-forest obstructions admitting jointly positive shared-row countermodels, without the forests becoming merely decorative generic algebraic witnesses. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the five-node active-deletion example where the pruned graph has no hedge but the empty trace has one, then test a local bow whose target becomes identified through an observed reference context; failure to reject the false local countermodel, or inability to link the surviving forest to query separation, forces a pivot or stop.
